**Fieldbook 2.1.2 beta 3** (a beta)
The third beta of 2.1.2, on the beta channel: Macs set to **Beta** (Settings › General › Updates › Versions) get it as an automatic update. Everyone else stays on 2.1.1 until 2.1.2 itself.
### Added - **Remove a speaker mark made by mistake:** while recording, each mark in the meeting's header has a **✕**; after the call, so does its ⚑ line in the transcript, and the mark's row under **Speakers** has **Remove** next to Yes and No. Right-clicking a mark offers **Remove Mark** too. - **Change a mark's name while recording:** click a mark in the meeting's header to open **Who's talking?** again and choose someone else (or **No Name**); **Escape** keeps it as it was.

**Fieldbook 2.1.2 beta 2** (a beta)
### Added - **A licensing library:** **Licensing**, at the bottom of the sidebar above **My To-dos**, keeps your own SKU sheets, feature matrices, price lists, licensing guides, and vendors' licensing web pages, and answers questions about them, such as which edition includes a feature or what else is needed above 5,000 users. Each point links to the row or page behind it (**L1**, **L2**, …): click to see the row with its columns, then **Open File** or **Copy Row**. Nothing is built in: each SE adds what they use, once, and the library stays through updates. - **Add File…** takes Excel, CSV, Word, PowerPoint, PDF, or text, with the company it's about (sources are grouped by company). Spreadsheets are read one row at a time with their column names, up to 20,000 rows a sheet. **Replace…** brings in a newer version. - **Ask AI uses the licensing library too:** a question in the toolbar's search field about licensing (a license, edition, SKU, tier, add-on, pricing, or what something includes) also gets the best matching rows and pages of your licensing sources, cited as **L1**, **L2**, … beside the meeting lines. - **Share the library:** the **⋯** menu in the Licensing list has **Share Library…**, one file with every source, and **Import Library…** for one a colleague shared (or drop it on the list). Their sources join yours; ones you already have are updated only by a newer copy. - **Licensing in AI notes:** when you have licensing sources, a meeting's opportunities are matched to them after its notes are written: under each opportunity, the SKUs, editions, or add-ons that fit and what else they need, linked to the rows behind them. **Match Licensing** (or **Match Again** after your sources change) does it on request. - **Add Link…** reads a web page, or the page and the pages under it (up to 50), from this Mac when you add it, and keeps a dated copy; **Refresh** reads it again. Fieldbook reads links only when you add or refresh them, over HTTPS, and respects the site's robots.txt.
### Changed - **The account summary reads the customer's opportunities:** "Where things stand" names each open one with its close quarter and stage, using your notes on it; a statement that comes from an opportunity lists it among its sources. Adding or changing an opportunity (its stage, quarter, status, name, or notes) marks the summary out of date, so **Update** brings it up to date with just that opportunity, and removing one asks for a rewrite.
### Fixed - **Update All counts an opportunity's changes right away:** after you edit an opportunity, the button (and the customer's **Update** line on its Account page) includes the account summary and that opportunity's MEDDPICC within a couple of seconds, instead of only after the next check a few minutes later or when Fieldbook comes to the front.

**Fieldbook 2.1.2 beta 1** (a beta)
The first beta of 2.1.2, on the beta channel: Macs set to **Beta** (Settings › General › Updates › Versions) get it as an automatic update. Everyone else stays on 2.1.1 until 2.1.2 itself.
### Added - **Opportunities for each customer:** a new **Opportunities** row under **Account** keeps each deal you track in Salesforce or your CRM, stacked one per line like a folder's emails: click one to open it with its close quarter (such as **Q2 FY27**), **Technical Validation Stage**, Open/Won/Lost, a link that opens it in your browser, and your notes, with **Copy** on every section to paste into the CRM. **New Opportunity…** starts one in this quarter. - **The recommended stage and MEDDPICC per opportunity,** from the meetings that count toward it, its notes and your account notes, and the customer's emails. Each customer meeting has an **Opportunity** menu next to its Brief (where the stage menu was); while a customer has one open opportunity, its meetings count toward it on their own. - **Next steps:** **Write** suggests an opportunity's open next steps from the briefs and to-dos of its meetings (crossed-off to-dos count as done) and its notes, each linked to the lines behind it. - **Suggested opportunities** from the opportunities in your meetings' AI notes: **Add…** starts one with its name, and the meetings it came up in count toward it. - **Links in your notes:** web and email addresses in your meeting notes, account notes, and opportunities' notes are links: click one to open it in your browser, or point at it to see where it goes. - **Settings › General › Opportunities › Fiscal year starts in** (August unless you change it), for close quarters. - **Import transcripts from Word:** **Import Transcript…** and dropping a file now take `.docx` transcripts, such as Teams' **Download as .docx** (newer files with "Name 0:03" before each turn, and older ones with "0:0:0.0 --> 0:0:5.1" timings), with their speakers and times. The meeting's title, date, and length at the top and Teams' "started transcription" lines are left out. A Word document without times still becomes a manual meeting with its text in your notes. (`.txt` transcripts, including Zoom's export, were already imported.)
### Changed - **The stage, MEDDPICC, and the recommended stage moved from meetings and the account to each opportunity.** The Account page starts with the customer's open opportunities, then account notes and the account summary. A customer whose meetings set a stage, or that had MEDDPICC, offers **Start an Opportunity with It…**, which brings both along. - **Update All** lists MEDDPICC per open opportunity, and the pre-call brief uses the open opportunity's MEDDPICC.
### Fixed - **Update All's button counts again after a run finishes in the background:** closing its window while it works no longer leaves the button saying "Updated" until you open it and choose Done; once the run ends, the button shows what's still out of date.

Offered to 1.8 and later as an automatic update, a small one from 2.1. Everything in the two betas of 2.1.1.
### Added
- **Mark who's talking:** while recording, press **Control-Option-S** (from any app), click **Mark Speaker** in the meeting's header, or use the menu-bar icon, and type who it is in the small **Who's talking?** box (people invited and people you've met are suggested; your call app stays in front; its **✕** closes it without marking). After transcription, the speaker talking then is offered that name with **Yes** and **No** under **Speakers**; a mark without a name lets you listen from that moment and name them. The transcript shows where you marked. Marks made in Fieldbook for iPhone come with its recordings and are offered the same way. - **Cross off to-dos:** click a to-do's icon in a meeting's notes when it's done, or when it doesn't apply. It stays in place, struck through; click again to put it back. Completing a to-do's reminder in Reminders crosses it off too. - **Correct and add to-dos:** the pencil beside a to-do fixes its words, kind, or owner when the AI or the transcript got something wrong (**Use AI's Wording** undoes it). **Add To-do** adds your own, with **Remind me** to add it to Reminders right away. What you change is kept when the notes are updated or regenerated, and Copy, the follow-up email, Ask AI, the account summary, and the pre-call brief use your version. - **My To-dos:** at the bottom of the sidebar, your open to-dos from every meeting (the ones whose owner is you), grouped by customer, with a **Completed** list of what you've crossed off. Click one to open its meeting at that to-do. - **Azure OpenAI as a cloud service:** **Settings › AI › Cloud endpoint › Service › Azure OpenAI (Microsoft Foundry)** takes your resource's endpoint (or just its name; Fieldbook adds `/openai/v1` and shows where requests go) and one of its keys, kept apart from a LiteLLM endpoint's. Models are your deployments' names: if one isn't listed, choose **Other…** and type it.
### Changed
- **No more pauses from Update All's check:** working out what Update All can bring up to date now reads meetings' notes in the background, and only those that changed since the last check, so Fieldbook doesn't pause for a moment every couple of minutes or when you switch to it. The button's count also stays current while you record. - **The follow-up email and Ask AI check their sources:** as AI notes do, each point now comes with a few words quoted from the line it cites, and Fieldbook checks they're really there. In a follow-up email, a paragraph whose quote isn't found is asked about again once, and if it still isn't found it's marked with an orange warning for you to check before sending (the mark isn't copied). In an Ask AI answer, a citation whose quote isn't found shows as **not found** instead of a link. - **Fewer stray words split off to the wrong speaker:** in fast exchanges, a word at the start or end of a line could be credited to the person before or after and shown as a one-word line of theirs. Words are now grouped at pauses and given to speakers a phrase at a time, so a speaker changes only where someone says more than a word or two, and a short reply between pauses still keeps its own speaker. For new transcriptions and **Detect Speakers Again**.

Offered to 1.8 and later as an automatic update. Everything since 2.0, including what the four betas brought (they were called 2.0.1 while they were tested).
### Added
- **Release or Beta, for everyone:** **Settings › General › Updates › Versions** (and the top of the Welcome window) offers **Release**, tested versions for most people, or **Beta**, new features first while they're still being tested. With Beta, each beta comes as an automatic update, as well as every full release. Choosing Release again keeps the version you have until the next release. A beta shows which it is, such as "Version 2.1.1 beta 1". - **Welcome to Fieldbook 2.1** opens once after updating: choose Release or Beta, and see everything new with where to find it. - **Emails for every folder:** customers, Internal, Training, Partners, and every label have an **Emails** row under **Files**: the folder's emails newest first, a reader with their attachments (a screenshot pasted into an email comes with them), **Open in Mail**, and an **Emails summary** linked to the emails behind each point. Click the open email's subject to fold it to one line. Add emails by dropping `.eml` files (Gmail's **⋮ › Download message**, or dragged from Mail or Outlook) or with **Add Emails…**. - **The email Inbox:** emails from your email folder (such as a Gmail label) wait in an **Inbox** instead of popping up, even during a call. The **Inbox** button at the top of the window, the Dock icon, and the menu-bar menu say how many; click it (or **File › Email Inbox…**, Shift-Command-E) to file each one as a new meeting or in a folder's **Emails**, where its people's domains suggest, in the background while you keep working. - **An email folder:** **Settings › General › Downloads and Email Folder › Email folder** watches a folder you choose, such as the Google Drive folder a Gmail label saves to, even while Fieldbook is closed. - **Emails become meetings:** drag an email from Mail or Outlook into Fieldbook, or download one from Gmail. The meeting is named from the subject and dated when it was sent, with who it's from and to and its text in your notes, the email and its attachments attached, and the folder its people's email domains point to chosen to begin with. - **Getting Emails into Fieldbook** in Help: every way to bring emails in, with step-by-step setup for a Gmail label (a script in a box that opens to show what it creates and does, with **Copy**), for flagging emails in Outlook with Microsoft 365 (a Power Automate flow), and for Apple Mail. - **The AI reads emails and attachments:** a meeting's AI notes read its attachments (emails, PDFs, Word, Excel, PowerPoint, text, and the words in screenshots, recognized on this Mac); a customer's MEDDPICC and recommended stage use its emails as evidence; **Ask AI** searches your folders' emails and can cite them; and emails kept in a folder's Files are read for the files summary, the account summary, and Account Discovery. - **Update All:** a button at the top of the window says how many AI notes, Discovery answers, MEDDPICC, and summaries have something new. Choose which to bring up to date (rewrites start unticked); they're done one at a time, sending only what's new where they can, and keep going when you close it. Anything that fails says why, with **Try Again** and **Try All Again**. Also **File › Update All…** (Shift-Command-U), and **Update <customer>…** on a customer's Account. - **Change a meeting's date and time:** click the date under its title, or right-click it in the list › **Change Date and Time…**. - **Drag a file into Fieldbook** to make a meeting from it, add it to a customer's Files, or attach it to a meeting: drop files anywhere in the window or on the Dock icon, or choose **File › Add Files…** (Shift-Command-A). A transcript becomes a meeting with its speakers and times; any other file becomes a manual meeting with the file attached and its text in your notes. Drop straight onto a customer in the sidebar or a meeting in the list, with **Undo**. - **Remind Me on to-dos:** click the bell at the end of a to-do to add it to Apple Reminders; the bell then shows when it's due, or **Done**. **New Reminder…** in a meeting's menu adds one for the meeting itself. - **Recordings AirDropped from the iPhone are imported by themselves** into the folder chosen on the phone, with **Undo** (Settings › General › Downloads), and **File › Send Folders to iPhone…** gives Fieldbook for iPhone your folders and the email domains that file meetings. - **Ask AI in Help:** type a question in Fieldbook Help's search field and press Return; the answer comes from the manual, with links to the sections it used. - **Microsoft Security** is back in **Settings › AI › Company and Solutions**, with its solutions list. Zscaler stays the default. - **Settings › Permissions lists the optional permissions** (Calendars, Reminders, the Downloads folder) with what each is for.
### Changed
- **A meeting's speakers are listed one per line,** most talk time first, with their side, whether their voice was recognized (or **Yes** and **No** for a suggested name), and how long they spoke. Click **Speakers** to fold the list. - **The account summary reads the account's emails and its meetings' attachments,** and **Update** sends just the new ones. Including the customer's other files stays your choice. - **The toolbar stays put:** **Notes | Transcript**, **Inbox**, and **Update All** are always in the same places, greyed out when they don't apply. - **Text size covers the meeting list and Help** too. - **The Welcome window is for anyone:** step 1 is **Bring your own AI**: Apple's on-device model, a local model, or a cloud model by API, with where Zscaler employees (their company's AI endpoint) and Microsoft employees (Azure OpenAI in Microsoft Foundry, under **LiteLLM or OpenAI-compatible**; Help says how) get theirs. - **Recordings from the iPhone arrive filed** in the folder chosen there; one sent without its audio becomes a notes-only meeting; sending one again after choosing its folder moves the copy on the Mac; and dragging a meeting export into Fieldbook imports it without asking where it goes.
### Fixed
- **Imported Zoom files are dated when the meeting was,** from Zoom's file names, instead of when they were imported, and named **Zoom chat**, **Zoom transcript**, or **Zoom captions**. - **Long AI replies no longer fail:** notes whose reply runs past the AI's length limit are written from smaller parts of the meeting, an update that runs too long is written in full, and Discovery asks about a long document's questions in smaller sets. A customer's Discovery reads every document even when one fails, and says which. - **Links in Ask AI and Help answers aren't clickable;** only the citation chips open. - **New Customer, New Label, and Email Domains and Addresses are readable** in light mode with a dark sidebar.

Offered to 1.8 and later as an automatic update. Everything since 1.9, including what the three betas brought.
### Added
- **Styles:** Settings › General › Look › **Style** offers twelve looks, each in light and dark: **Fieldbook** (the new standard: cream paper, kraft brown, serif headings, ruled lines under your notes), **Fieldbook Legacy** (the 1.x look), Cyber, Blueprint, Solarized, Graphite, Forest, Orchid, Cyberpunk, Matrix, Medieval, and Sci-Fi. **Two-tone** (on by default) puts the sidebar and toolbar in the style's cover color; selected rows take the style's color after **Reopen Fieldbook**; **Font** (also the **Aa** button above your notes) sets the font for notes and transcripts. - **Welcome to Fieldbook 2.0** opens once after updating: pick a look, and see everything new with where to find it. - **Mute Fieldbook:** muting Zoom or Teams doesn't mute your Mac's microphone, so Fieldbook can now be muted itself, with **Control-Option-Command-M**, **Mute** in the Recorder or the toolbar, or the menu-bar icon. Silence is recorded in place of your microphone, a "Fieldbook is muted" panel stays on screen, the call's audio keeps recording, and anything said while muted is left out of the transcript. - **Level meters and microphone warnings** in the Recorder: both tracks' levels while recording, and a warning at once when your microphone clips, is too quiet, or delivers no sound, with what to do. A microphone that delivers nothing is started again after 4 seconds. - **Choose the microphone in the Recorder:** it names the microphone Fieldbook will record; click it to pick another, before or during a recording. - The meeting header names every microphone recorded, in the order used ("Microphone: 33:12 (Rode NT-USB)"), with notes such as AirPods being in headset mode during the call. - **Merge Meetings…** (right-click two or more recordings): a meeting recorded in parts, or started on the iPhone and finished on the Mac, becomes one meeting, transcribed again as a whole, with the joins marked and the originals in the Trash. - **Space** plays and pauses a meeting's audio (not while you type). - **Speakers:** **Add Speaker…** for someone the transcription missed, click a paragraph's name to give it to someone else, **People you've met** suggested from remembered voices, and **Detect Speakers Again…** with how many people spoke on each track. - **Account Discovery:** a **Discovery** row under each customer's Account shows every discovery question with the answer from all of its meetings, account notes, files, and attachments, with sources and dates, earlier or differing answers, filters, and **Copy All**. Pre-call briefs leave out questions already answered. - **Update** instead of a full rewrite for AI notes (**Update Notes**), account summaries, MEDDPICC, and files summaries: when something was only added, only that is sent to your AI endpoint, for far fewer tokens (cloud endpoints). - Discovery questions are numbered as in Salesforce (Q1 to Q253), in each meeting, the brief, **Copy**, and CSV export and import. - **Where each meeting is filed:** its folder and label after the title, in the folders' colors, with **Move To** beside them, and a short path before each title in All Meetings and Archive. - **Arrow keys:** Right goes from the folders to the meetings, then from Notes to Transcript; Left goes back. Right on a folder with hidden labels opens it first, and Left closes it. - Recordings paused on the iPhone (Fieldbook for iPhone) show how long they were paused, and nothing from the paused time is transcribed.
### Changed
- The microphone is recorded through a capture session bound to that one device, so changing headphones or the Mac's output can no longer interrupt it. - With no call, Fieldbook doesn't record a nearby iPhone's microphone on its own unless it's the only one. A microphone you picked is noted as "the microphone you chose". - Set up for Zscaler: a new install goes straight to the Zscaler setup steps, with Zscaler's AI endpoint filled in, `zscaler.com` as your domain, and Company and Solutions preloading Zscaler. Settings already saved don't change. - Discovery costs less: only new questions are matched (**Match Them**, **Update All**), renames don't make it out of date, and with Claude (a Claude API key or a LiteLLM proxy) the question list is read from Claude's prompt cache; Settings › AI › Usage shows how much came from the cache. - MEDDPICC's refresh after a new customer meeting adds only that meeting's evidence, and skips a meeting with nothing to read. - Renaming a speaker or the meeting no longer makes AI notes or Discovery out of date; the new names go into the notes without the AI. - Automatic AI notes are skipped for a meeting with an empty transcript and no notes of yours (**Write Notes** still works). - A meeting always opens on **Notes**; a search result or citation opens the transcript at its line. - The red REC timer in the toolbar is a Stop button. - Help covers everything new, including **Merging Recordings**, **Updating Instead of Rewriting**, **Recordings from your iPhone**, and how to send a meeting with its audio along with a diagnostic report. - Settings › AI's data notice says that meeting attachments' text is sent when you choose **Update** in a customer's Discovery.
### Fixed
- Transcription could hang for good on some completely silent recordings, at every launch. Fieldbook now reads recordings in small pieces, and a meeting cut off twice waits for **Retry Transcription**. - A track that ends before you stop recording is filled with silence to the end. - Importing an export checks each audio track's file name, so a hand-edited export can't point Fieldbook outside the meeting's folder. - On macOS 26, a light frame no longer shows around the sidebar's color. - MEDDPICC no longer fails when a customer has a meeting with nothing to read, such as a silent test recording.
### Since beta 3 (build 21)
- In the sidebar, **Right** on a folder with hidden labels (such as Partners) opens it first; **Right** again moves to the meetings. **Left** closes an open folder. - A microphone you picked yourself, in the Recorder or in Settings, is noted as "the microphone you chose" (it said "chosen in Settings" even when picked in the Recorder). - A meeting's header names every microphone it was recorded from, in the order used, not only the last one; a merged meeting lists all of its parts' microphones. - **Welcome to Fieldbook 2.0** also lists the Recorder's microphone menu, each meeting's folder path, and the arrow keys. - Fixed: MEDDPICC failed when a customer had a meeting with nothing to read, such as a silent test recording moved there; it now skips that meeting, as automatic notes do. - Fixed: following the call app's microphone was logged as a warning ("microphone interrupted") in the activity log; real interruptions still are. - Fixed: on macOS 26, a light frame showed around the sidebar's cover color (macOS 26 floats the sidebar a little in from the window's edges, and the meeting list's color showed around it); the sidebar's own color now fills that space, also in the Help window.
